writeup: TIC 447009429 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 8.001809 days and a primary eclipse depth of 13.69 percent dimming. The detection carries a high signal-to-noise ratio of 554.2 from the automated periodogram search, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms the source at a signal-to-noise ratio of 133.4, though with a centroid offset of 2.6 arcseconds from the target position. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown candidate. A secondary eclipse was not detected in the data. One open question remains: the eclipse depths alternate significantly between consecutive orbital cycles, which may indicate physical variability in the system or suggest orbital dynamics worth investigating further.
